answer: A registry can require every new agent to earn a slow, decaying reputation balance before it may transact: it starts by completing small verifiable jobs for established agents, and each completed job adds credit that fades unless renewed by further honest work. Like a tide, trust rises only gradually and falls back without upkeep; a Sybil attacker faces a spiral of effort, since each fake identity must separately grind through the same months of work, while a nebula of sock puppets with no history stays dark and untrusted, unable to move value.
